JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Venkataramaiah, who is husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioners No.2 to 6, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
Susheelamma vs Commissioner Cmc on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188011316/
2
On 26-02-2025, at about 5.45 a.m., beside R.K. Hardware, Lakshmipura, Bengaluru City, when the deceased Venkataramaiah was proceeding as pedestrian at the road side near Lakshmipura.

At that time one Intra V 30 Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52- B-5423 came from behind i.e. from Lakshmipura towards Madanayakanahalli, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and then he was shifted to ESI Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment and then he was shifted to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he died while undergoing treatment.

Earlier to the accident the deceased was working as Curb Operator in SLV Concrete Product, Lakshmipura road,
Dasanapura Hobli, Nelamangala and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Madanayakanahally Police have registered the case against the driver of the said vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 125(a) and 281 of BNS.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, at the time of accident the driver of his goods carrier was driving the same cautiously, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.
He has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

Further, he has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant and the vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423 was insured with the respondent No.2 vide policy No.20230823154105 and the same was valid from 26-01-2025 to 25-01-2026.
The driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
There is no violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1.
As such, in view of indemnity contract/insurance, the respondent No.2 is statutorily and legally liable to reimburse the respondent No.1 in terms of the conditions of the policy.

For the above denials and contentions,
he prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
It has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further it is contended that, the Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle was proceeding from Lakshmipura towards Madanayakanahalli.

During the process of driving the said vehicle reverse on the said road, with due care, caution and observing all traffic rules and regulations, the deceased suddenly came behind the vehicle and it led to the alleged accident.

As a result he fell down and sustained alleged injuries and Susheelamma vs Commissioner Cmc on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188011316/
3 succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment.
Further it is contended that, due to contributory negligence of the deceased the alleged accident has occurred.
At no point of time the driver of Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle had driven the same in rash and negligent manner.
The petitioners have filed false complaint against the driver of the said vehicle to make wrongful gain from this respondent.
Further it is contended that, the vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423 is insured with the respondent No.2 under "P" policy which was in force from 26-01-2025 to 25-01- 2026.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Venkataramaiah S/o Late Cheluvaiah has succumbed to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident,
alleged to have been occurred on 26-02-2025, at about 5.45 a.m., on Lakshmipura,
beside of R.K. Hardware, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Intra V 30 vehicle bearing registration No.KA-52-B-5423 ?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
7. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.2 has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked total 34 documents as Ex.P.1 to 34.
On the other hand, the respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 26-02-2025, at about 5.45 a.m., beside R.K. Hardware, Lakshmipura, Bengaluru City, when the deceased Venkataramaiah was proceeding as a pedestrian from extreme side of the road, at that time the driver of offending Intra V 30 Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-5423, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased from behind.
Due to the said impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.

Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident the deceased was working as Curb Operator in SLV Concrete Product, Lakshmipura road,
Susheelamma vs Commissioner Cmc on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188011316/
4 Dasanapura Hobli, Nelamangala and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.2 has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 34 documents as Ex.P.1 to 34.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of requisition letter of I.O., Ex.P.4 is true copy of further statement of complainant, Ex.P.5 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.7 is true copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.8 is true copy of inquest, Ex.P.9 is true copy of post- mortem report, Ex.P.10 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.11 is true copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.12 is true copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.13 is true copy of statement of accused, Ex.P.14 are true copy of statement of witnesses (total 2), Ex.P.15 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.16 is salary certificate, Ex.P.17 to 23 are notarized copy of Aadhar cards of petitioners No.1 to 6 and deceased, Ex.P.24 to 28 are notarized copy of PAN cards of petitioners No.1 to 4 and Ex.P.29 to 34 are notarized copy of bank pass book of petitioners No.1 to 6.
12.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 15, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423 and dashing the same to the deceased pedestrain from behind.
Due to said impact the deceased Venkataramaiah has sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment in Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.15, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, due to negligence of the deceased the alleged accident has taken place.

The Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle was proceeding from Lakshmipura towards Madanayakanahalli and during the process of driving the said vehicle in reverse direction with due care, caution and observing all traffic rules and regulations, the deceased suddenly came behind the vehicle and led to alleged accident.

Further it is contended that, at no point of time the driver of Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle had drone the same in rash and negligent manner and the petitioners with a sole intention to have wrongful gain from the respondents have lodged a false complaint against the driver of the said vehicle, in collusion with the police authorities.
But, they have failed to establish the said contentions.
The respondents No.1 and 2 have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to show that, the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
Even they have not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record Susheelamma vs Commissioner Cmc on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188011316/
5 by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423 and dashing the same to the deceased Venkataramaiah from behind.

Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to the negligence of the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.5 spot mahazar and Ex.P.6 also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 30 feet wide Lakshmipura- Madanayakanahalli road, infront of R.K.
Hardware, Lakshmipura Village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, in between the offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423 and the deceased Venkataramaiah, who was pedestrian on the said road.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.12, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.15 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-542 and the deceased has succumbed to fatal injuries sustained in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA- 52-B-542 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, injuries caused to deceased Venkataramaiah in the said accident and the cause of his death.
15. Further, the Ex.P.9 Post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Venkataramaiah has died due to head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the documents produced by the petitioners are false.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-542, injuries caused to deceased Venkataramaiah in the said accident and cause of his death.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text:
18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Venkataramaiah has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, occurred on 26-02-2025 at about 5:45 a.m., on Lakshmipura-Madanayakanahalli road, infront of R.K. Hardware, Lakshmipura Village,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Intra V 30 Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-B-5423.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Intra V 30 Nagarasabhe Thyajya Vilevari vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-52- B-5423 and deceased Venkataramaiah has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident and succumbed to said injuries,
while undergoing treatment at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In this regard, they have produced their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of deceased Venkataramaiah, which are marked as Ex.P.17 to 23.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioners No.2 to 6 are children of deceased Venkataramaiah.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Venkataramaiah is not specifically denied by the respondents No.1 and 2 in the case and even there is no rebuttal evidence with respect to same placed on record by the respondents No.1 and 2.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Venkataramaiah.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.

Susheelamma vs Commissioner Cmc on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188011316/
7
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
21.

According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.

22. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Venkataramaiah and they were depending on him.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
23. Age and income of the deceased:
The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 70 years.
To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Venkataramaiah, which is marked as Ex.P.17, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01-02-1955.
The accident has taken place on 26-02-2025.
This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 70 years.

The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as Curb Operator in SLV Concrete Product, Lakshmipura road, Dasanapura Hobli, Nelamangala and was earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.
To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the salary certificate, which is marked as Ex.P.16.
But, they have not examined the author of the document, to prove the contents and authenticity of said document.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners have failed to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, as on the date of accident.
As such, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

24. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another,
in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."

8 25.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2025.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be treated as Rs.17,000/- per month.
Therefore, the annual income of the deceased in the present case is held as Rs.2,04,000/-.
26. Future prospects:
As on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 70 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are not entitled for future prospects of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 27. The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of 6 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 to 6.
The total number of the dependents of the deceased are six.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 1/4th of the total income, which comes to Rs.51,000/-.

After deducting 1/4th out of total income, towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.1,53,000/-.
28.
As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 70 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 5.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is held as Rs.1,53,000/- x 5 = Rs.7,65,000/-.
29.
Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioners No.2 to 6 are children of deceased Venkataramaiah.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 to 6 are entitled for compensation under the head of spousal and parental consortium.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
b ) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/-
 c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-
30.
The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of spousal and parental consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioners No.1 to 6 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.

31. Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:

No. Compensation

2. Loss of spousal and Rs. 2,88,000-00  parental consortium

Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,89,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
32. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B- 5423.

Further, as per the true copy of reply given by the owner of offending vehicle, to the notice issued by the investigation officer under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, which is marked as Ex.P.11, the driver of offending vehicle by name Dayanandamurthy S/o Beerayya was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA5220130000946 and it was valid from 16-02-2013 to 15-02-2033 and the offending vehicle was insured by respondent No.2 insurance company vide policy bearing No.1307947 and it was valid from 26-01-2025 to 25-01-2026.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 26-02-2025.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5423, the accident has occurred and the deceased Venkataramaiah has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,89,000/- from the respondent No.2, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
33. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

10
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.10,89,000/- (Rupees ten lakh eighty nine thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA- 52-B-542 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, injuries caused to deceased Venkataramaiah in the said accident and the cause of his death.
15. Further, the Ex.P.9 Post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Venkataramaiah has died due to head injury sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the documents produced by the petitioners are false.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-542, injuries caused to deceased Venkataramaiah in the said accident and cause of his death.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
22. The compensation towards loss of dependency: The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Venkataramaiah and they were depending on him.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners have failed to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, as on the date of accident.
